transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jonah Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Kapoor (CTO, Suncrest), Evan Liu (Infra Eng), Marta Reyes (Compliance)
Shared links: redwood-private-deploy-playbook.pdf (Redwood), security-whitepaper-suncrest.pdf (customer), benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx (referenced)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Suncrest evaluating air-gapped on-prem inference. Primary concerns: hardware SKU and driver compatibility, offline update mechanics (signed bundles / sneakernet), key management (HSM), audit and patch windows, and fallback behavior. Next: SE to provide compatibility matrix and offline update playbook; AVA to send SOC2/security artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Ava with Redwood, and Jonah here is our SE.
[00:09] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Hi, yes thanks. We appreciate the time. We wanted to use this call to walk through how you do fully-isolated deployments, and how we would keep things patched given our regulatory windows.
[00:18] Jonah (Redwood SE): Great. High level we'll cover hardware, image signing and updates, KMS/HSM integration, and maintenance windows. I'll also show where hosted/dedicated differs but we recognize you can't phone-home from the cluster.
[00:28] Evan Liu: Just to set expectations — our network is air-gapped. No outbound to public internet. We have an internal depot that only accepts signed images. We also have change windows twice a quarter.
[00:36] Jonah: Good callout. How long are your maintenance windows?
[00:40] Evan Liu: Typically 4 hours, two times per quarter. Emergency patches used but need approval.
[00:44] Marta Reyes: And compliance wants full audit trail for any image or model change, plus HSM-based key custody. SOC2/ISO references matter.
[00:52] Ava: Understood. We'll map that to our private deployment model. Quick question on GPU preference — are you targeting large A100/H100 clusters or something smaller?
[01:03] Dr. Priya Kapoor: We're experimenting. Models will range from smaller retrieval augmented generation endpoints for clinical search to larger reasoning models for protocol drafting. Likely mix: H100 for heavy offline batches, and A10/A40 class for lower-latency services due to budget.
[01:18] Jonah: That mix is fine. We'll provide SKU guidance. For H100s you get better perf on high-seq models; A10/A40 are cost-effective for many LLMs. We also recommend validated driver/kernel versions — we send a compatibility matrix.
[01:30] Evan Liu: Important: our fleet runs RHEL 8.8 with a custom kernel; we can't upgrade kernel without validation.
[01:35] Jonah: Noted — we'll include kernel/driver permutations. The runtime is fairly tolerant but GPU driver/kernel mismatches can break NVLINK or MPS.
[01:44] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Talk to me through updates. We can't just let a cluster phone home and pull latest images, so how do you do air-gap updates?
[01:52] Jonah: Two main patterns we've used: 1) sealed, signed bundle approach — we produce a signed tarball (image + manifests + signature) you ingest via your internal depot. Signing keys are in HSM and you verify on the host. 2) Sneakernet (sorry, I said sneaker-net yesterday) — USB/secure transfer with attestation. Both require image signing and a reproducible hash.
[02:10] Marta Reyes: We like the HSM approach; also need RBAC mapping so only a small ops group can approve pushing to depot.
[02:16] Ava: On the signing piece we can integrate with your HSM via PKCS11 or with an offline attestation service. We also support a customer-managed KMS for encrypting model weights at rest.
[02:26] Evan Liu: Can Redwood's private control plane be deployed in our VPC, or does it remain with you?
[02:31] Jonah: For fully air-gapped, control plane can be customer-hosted. We ship a management bundle that runs in your admin network — it doesn't need outbound internet if you don't want. There is a thin operator component that you host.
[02:42] Dr. Priya Kapoor: If the control plane is on-prem, then how does Redwood handle telemetry and traces? We need audit copies but nothing leaves the perimeter.
[02:50] Jonah: Telemetry can be written to an internal S3-compatible store you host. We also can provide locator tooling to emit JSON logs to your SIEM. Nothing needs to go to Redwood unless you permit it.
[03:00] Evan Liu: That model works. Now, licensing — do we need to commit to dedicated capacity, or can we run the runtime against our own infra without a capacity commitment?
[03:09] Ava: For private on-prem, pricing is an enterprise license + support. Dedicated contracts are more for reserved pools in our managed offering. We'll be flexible: licensing fee for the private bundle and optional support tiers. Jonah, can you speak to what telemetry we require for monetization?
[03:21] Jonah: Essentially an install receipt and periodic heartbeat is enough for license management; that too can be one-way to your license server. We can do offline license validation — signed license file you host.
[03:30] Marta Reyes: On the security front, what about model provenance — how do we prove model weights haven't been tampered with?
[03:36] Jonah: We recommend binary signing of model artifacts and storing SHA256 digests in an attestation ledger. If you need, we can integrate with Sigstore-style transparency logs, or provide local-only attestations that live in your vault.
[03:49] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Great. Performance: A bit worried about latency with on-prem quantized models and caching. How do you handle KV cache and batching without outbound routing?
[03:58] Jonah: The runtime supports local KV cache (we had a transcribe glitch in our docs where KV cache was 'K-V cash'), and continuous batching within the cluster. For cold starts we recommend prefix caching and warm pools. In an air-gapped setup, warm pools are pre-provisioned.
[04:12] Evan Liu: Do you support INT8/4-bit quantized kernels? Our finance team likes the cost delta.
[04:16] Jonah: Yes — quantization profiles are supported but we need to validate accuracy for your model mix. Some kernels prefer specific CUDA/cuDNN versions. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the matrix.
[04:26] Ava: Also worth noting we have a Redwood Optimize report that can suggest batching/caching/quantization to hit cost+latency goals. We'll tailor that to your workload once we have telemetry.
[04:36] Dr. Priya Kapoor: What's your fallback behavior if a node loses model integrity or a kernel panics?
[04:41] Jonah: For private, we rely on your orchestration — we provide health checks and safe rollback artifacts. If we detect model corruption, the runtime can drop to a read-only mode and run a smaller model, but because you're air-gapped there's no remote fallback to hosted. We can supply a tested fallback image you store locally.
[04:58] Evan Liu: Interesting. We need clear rollback playbooks that align with our change window and we want automatic validation so we don't ship a bad image.
[05:06] Jonah: Agreed — update playbook will include preflight tests, canary steps (within an air-gapped cluster), verification checksums and an approval gating step. We'll outline the canary pattern that fits within your 4-hour window.
[05:18] Marta Reyes: From compliance — we need to know how long logs are kept, encryption at rest, and who signs off on production rollouts.
[05:25] Ava: We support retention policies local to your S3 store; encryption at rest with your KMS/HSM; and RBAC mapping so Marta's team can be approvers.
[05:33] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Any gotchas around firmware or BIOS updates?
[05:36] Jonah: Firmware updates are vendor-specific and usually outside of Redwood's direct control. We will catalog vendor recommendations and note which driver updates are required for certain kernels. We'll include firmware advisory notes in the compatibility matrix.
[05:47] Evan Liu: For benchmarking we want to run a 24-hour throughput test and a 99th percentile latency. Can Redwood provide reproducible bench scripts that run offline?
[05:56] Jonah: Yes — we have a bench harness you can run locally that logs latencies and token throughput, and generates a CSV. We'll provide runner scripts and suggested load patterns.
[06:06] Dr. Priya Kapoor: On the legal side: do you support data residency controls and model usage restrictions? We cannot have PHI leave the cluster.
[06:13] Ava: For private on-prem, PHI never leaves the cluster unless you explicitly export. We can include contract language and security addendum.
[06:20] Evan Liu: One more technical nit: how do we manage secrets for model weights and tokenization assets?
[06:26] Jonah: Secrets are encrypted with your KMS; at runtime the process pulls keys from a local HSM via PKCS11. We also support ephemeral keys for session-level encryption.
[06:36] Marta Reyes: We're also worried about people accidentally pushing models with PII into training or into the model registry. Do you provide scanning?
[06:42] Jonah: We have an optional vetting step — static scanning for PII artifacts and a policy engine that can block unapproved artifacts. In an air-gapped install, that runs on-prem as part of the preflight.
[06:52] Ava: Quick recap of what we'll deliver next: Jonah will do the HW/driver matrix + offline update playbook. I'll send SOC2/materials and pricing outline. We'll propose a site visit for the feasibility workshop.
[07:02] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. One more question — if we want a hybrid approach where some workloads run in your hosted environment for burst capacity, but core PHI stays on-prem, is that possible?
[07:11] Jonah: You can do policy-based routing, but for PHI you'd need explicit DLP and consent. We can route non-sensitive anonymized workloads to hosted. However, because your environment is air-gapped, automated burst is not trivial — you'd need a data egress path and approvals.
[07:25] Evan Liu: For now our compliance team says no outbound egress, so we'll keep everything local.
[07:29] Ava: Perfectly understood. We'll map next steps accordingly.
[07:33] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[07:36] Jonah: I'll include a sample signed-bundle verifier and a sample license file.
[07:40] Marta Reyes: Please also include a sample audit log format so our SIEM ingestors can be prepped.
[07:45] Ava: We'll do that. Any other questions?
[07:49] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Not right now. Thanks both.
[07:52] Ava: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and lock the workshop date.
[07:57] Evan Liu: Thanks.

Closing notes (auto): Meeting ended around 15:54 PDT. Participants agreed on deliverables and a feasibility workshop.
